headline: A law lets landowners in the Northport Irrigation District in Nebraska repay their share of federal water project construction costs early, which can lift certain federal reclamation law limits on their land.
what_it_does: Any landowner in the Northport Irrigation District can pay off, at any time, the construction costs of project facilities assigned to their land. Once all of those costs are paid in full, the land is no longer subject to federal reclamation law's ownership and full-cost pricing limits. On request, the Department of the Interior must give the landowner a certificate confirming the land is free of those limits.

who_it_affects.group: Landowners within the Northport Irrigation District in Nebraska
who_it_affects.how: They may choose to repay their share of project construction costs early and, after full payment, may be free of federal ownership and full-cost pricing limits on their land.
It must provide a certificate, on request, to a landowner who has fully repaid the construction costs, confirming the land is free of those limits.

when_it_takes_effect: The summary gives no separate start date, so the law took effect when it was enacted on January 10, 2019.
